LESSON: CLIMATIC REGIONS IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and the Built Environments
Topic 1.3: Climatic regions in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Climatic regions in Eastern Africa, part of Natural and the Built Environments in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: howing the main climatic regions, 1.How does climate influence our day-to- day activities? 2.Why are there different climatic regions in Eastern Africa?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Climatic regions in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: Learners observe safety precautions and practices as they use digital devices/print resources to draw the

main climatic regions of Eastern Africa.

• Communication and Collaboration: Learners recognise the value of others’ ideas as they discuss, in groups, the

characteristics of climatic regions in Eastern Africa.

Values:
Social justice: Learners accord equal opportunities in sharing responsibilities as they compose poems that address effects of

climatic change on human activities.

Love: Learners portray a caring attitude as they use digital devices to find out how climate influences human activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Disaster Risk Reduction: Learners are equipped with knowledge on disaster risk reduction as they compose poems

that address effects of climatic change on human activities.

• Decision making: Learners are able to make choices as they use digital/print media to find out how climate

influences human activities.

10

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Learners use English, Kiswahili and KSL skills as they recite poems on the importance of historic built environments.

• Learners apply Creative Arts skills to model a map of Eastern Africa showing the main climatic regions climatic regions.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Maps of Eastern Africa, tactile maps of Eastern Africa, audio-visual clips on formation of the main physical features in Eastern

Africa, recorded computer games on latitudes and longitudes, digital devices with assistive technology and approved appropriate

print or braille Social Studies textbooks.
